Home/IoT sensors/Vibration sensor

High-frequency
vibration sensor. Machine vibration.
Connected to your team.

The Hitelecom H Series vibration sensor combines a cabled external probe with a wireless terminal for high-frequency machinery monitoring. Mount the probe on a rigid motor bearing-housing point and send configured readings to your maintenance team. Select single-axis or triaxial sensing, with a vibration velocity RMS range of 0–50 mm/s, a display resolution of 0.1 mm/s and a measurement frequency range of 10–5,000 Hz. Match 4G, NB-IoT or LoRa connectivity and the reporting profile to your installation.

KEY FEATURES

Machine vibration.
Connected to maintenance.

Bring a machine-mounted probe, a suitable measurement profile and a wireless data connection into one monitoring workflow.

Probe at the machine

Place the cabled external probe at the selected mechanical point while locating the terminal for practical access and radio coverage.

Vibration velocity RMS

Measure vibration velocity RMS from 0–50 mm/s with a display resolution of 0.1 mm/s. Choose single-axis or triaxial sensing for the machine and measurement objective.

10–5,000 Hz measurement range

Monitor machinery vibration within a 10–5,000 Hz measurement frequency range. Match the probe mounting and acquisition profile to the frequencies relevant to your equipment.

Wireless remote reporting

Use the supplied 4G, NB-IoT or LoRa variant to connect distributed measurement points to the agreed monitoring platform.

Configured alert workflow

Define project thresholds, notification recipients and the inspection response around the selected metric and normal operating conditions.

Practical device setup

NFC activation, local configuration and OTA updates are listed for the family. Confirm the functions available on the supplied model.

MEASURE THE RIGHT QUANTITY

A clear quantity.
A repeatable measurement point.

A useful machine trend starts with a repeatable point, a clearly defined value and the operating conditions behind it. Agree these together before selecting the probe and reporting profile.

01↗

Vibration velocity RMS

Root mean square (RMS) vibration velocity is expressed in mm/s. The measurement range is 0–50 mm/s, with a display resolution of 0.1 mm/s. Compare readings at the same machine point under comparable operating conditions.

Define your measurement
Single-axis or triaxial · Mounting point · Operating speed · Normal baseline
Discuss this measurement ↗
02↔

Measurement frequency range

The specified measurement frequency range is 10–5,000 Hz. This describes the vibration frequencies measured by the probe; choose the wireless reporting interval separately to suit your maintenance workflow.

Define your measurement
Relevant machine frequencies · Probe mounting · Acquisition profile · Reporting interval
Discuss this measurement ↗
03↓

Operating context

Machine speed, load and production stage give each comparison its context. Capture these in the monitoring plan or available site records.

RPM range · Load state · Production cycle · Normal baseline

SENSING & INSTALLATION

Probe on the machine.
Terminal at a suitable location.

Mount the external probe directly on an approved rigid motor bearing housing or end-shield measurement pad near the selected bearing. Choose the sensing direction for a single-axis configuration, or define the three-axis orientation for a triaxial configuration. Secure the probe cable with suitable strain relief, clear of rotating parts and hot surfaces. Mount the wireless terminal separately within its environmental limits and verify coverage at that position. Follow the supplied probe mounting method, cable specification and installation drawing.

FROM READING TO RESPONSE

Measure at the machine.
Report to your team.

Acquisition defines how vibration is measured; reporting defines when the terminal sends data. Set the measurement band, acquisition requirements, reporting interval and alert response as one operating profile.

01

Measure

The external probe measures at the labelled machine point. Match the supplied measurement quantity, frequency band and acquisition settings to the monitoring objective.

02

Report

The terminal sends the configured readings through the selected cellular or LoRa connection. Agree the reporting schedule and complete platform path.

03

Review & respond

Compare like operating states, review configured notifications and give the maintenance team an agreed inspection step. Record the result for the next comparison.

PUBLISHED BATTERY-LIFE DESIGNOver 10 years.
At one-hour reporting.

The published battery-life reference exceeds 10 years at one-hour reporting under specified conditions. This reference belongs to the configured terminal operating profile. Actual life depends on the supplied battery, probe and acquisition duty, reporting schedule, radio coverage, retransmissions and temperature. Request the life estimate for the complete configuration you intend to deploy.

ANSWERS FOR YOUR PROJECT

Frequently
asked questions.

Answers for specifying machinery measurement, planning the cabled probe installation and connecting readings to the maintenance workflow.

Ask about your project ↗
What does the Hitelecom machinery vibration sensor measure?+

The Hitelecom H Series uses a cabled external probe for high-frequency machinery vibration monitoring. Vibration velocity is reported as a root mean square (RMS) value over a 0–50 mm/s range, with a display resolution of 0.1 mm/s. The specified measurement frequency range is 10–5,000 Hz. Select single-axis or triaxial sensing for the machine and mounting point, then configure the wireless reporting profile.

Where should a vibration probe be mounted on an electric motor?+

Mount the probe directly on an approved rigid part of the motor bearing housing or end shield, close to the bearing being monitored. Use the supplied mounting method and a prepared measurement surface. Record the point identifier and the single-axis direction or triaxial orientation. Secure the cable and locate the wireless terminal separately for access and radio coverage.

Which industrial machines are suitable for this monitoring approach?+

Common project candidates include electric motors, pumps, fans, compressors, gearboxes, conveyors, machine-tool spindles, mixers and centrifuges. Select a rigid, stationary measurement point near the component of interest, and match the supplied probe’s usable frequency band, range and installation conditions to the machine. This external-probe family is intended for high-frequency machinery vibration monitoring.

How does a wired probe work with a wireless monitoring terminal?+

The probe cable connects the mechanical measurement point to the monitoring terminal. The configured 4G, NB-IoT or LoRa connection handles the remote data link. Plan the probe position, approved cable length and terminal location together, considering machine access, cable protection and radio coverage.

What is the vibration measurement frequency range?+

The specified measurement frequency range is 10–5,000 Hz. This is the vibration frequency range measured at the probe, rather than a wireless reporting rate. The 80 Hz calibration condition is a separate calibration reference. Share the machine speed, target components and mounting arrangement so the acquisition and reporting profile can be matched to the application.

Does the sensor support single-axis or triaxial vibration measurement?+

Yes. Single-axis and triaxial configurations are available. A single-axis configuration measures vibration along its selected sensing direction. A triaxial configuration measures along three axes at the same mounting point. Specify the configuration and mounting orientation for your machine; the vibration velocity RMS display resolution is 0.1 mm/s.

How should readings be compared on variable-speed or cyclic machines?+

Record the machine's speed, load and operating stage with the monitoring plan. Establish comparable baselines for the states that matter, such as a stable running speed or a repeatable production-cycle phase. Review changes against those conditions and the maintenance history so the trend supports a focused inspection.

What helps preserve a useful high-frequency measurement?+

Use the approved mounting method on a clean, flat, rigid measurement surface. Mechanical coupling affects the mounted frequency response, so the sensor interface and any mounting base should be reviewed for the target band. Secure the cable with strain relief and suitable slack, and route it safely around moving parts and motor-power wiring.

How can vibration trends support the maintenance workflow?+

Agree a normal operating baseline, the values to review and a practical inspection response. A sustained change at a labelled measurement point can help the team prioritise checks and compare readings before and after maintenance. Detailed fault interpretation depends on the machine, the available measurement data and the analysis method used in the project.

What information helps Hitelecom prepare a suitable configuration?+

Share the machine type, speed range, operating cycle, target components, photos of the proposed mounting points and whether you need single-axis or triaxial measurement. Include the environment, cable-route requirements, measurement/reporting intervals, country and preferred platform or communications link. These details help align the probe, terminal and data requirements with your installation.
